## Reviewer 1

### Summary

This paper addresses the challenge of predictive uncertainty calibration in unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA). It introduces a post-hoc calibration framework called Pseudo-Cal, which leverages inference-stage mixup to synthesize a labeled pseudo-target set that mimics the correct-wrong statistics of real target samples. By transforming the unsupervised calibration problem into a supervised one, Pseudo-Cal can be effectively solved using temperature scaling. The proposed method is evaluated across various UDA scenarios, including closed-set, partial-set, source-free UDA, and semantic segmentation, demonstrating superior performance in reducing miscalibration.

3 good

### Presentation

3 good

### Contribution

2 fair

### Strengths

1. The paper is well-written and easy to follow.
2. The proposed method is simple and effective.
3. The experimental evaluation is comprehensive, spanning multiple UDA scenarios and comparing against a range of baselines.
